title: Doubling gravity would make terrestrial animals short-legged or serpent-like

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Doubling gravity would make terrestrial animals short-legged or serpent-like

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The form and actions of terrestrial animals are conditioned by the strength of gravity: if it were doubled, bipedal form would fail and most land animals would resemble short-legged saurians or serpents; if halved, animals would be lighter, more active and need less heart, lungs and blood.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Were the force of gravity to be doubled, our bipedal form would be a failure, and the majority of terrestrial animals would resemble short-legged saurians, or else serpents.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter II, “On Magnitude”; topic “Gravity conditions bodily form”. Scope: terrestrial animals

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch02-11: needs-new-data, resolvability 0.34

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The claim has measurable consequences after substantial interpretation, but the decisive counterfactual gravity regimes have not been observed over development and evolution. Existing altered-gravity data are too restricted to resolve the stated terrestrial morphology predictions.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: A direct test would compare terrestrial lineages evolving or developing under otherwise similar but different gravity, measuring posture, limb length, locomotor performance and cardiopulmonary investment. Existing Earth data can test gravity-load mechanics but not the predicted whole-fauna response to doubled or halved gravity.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Predictions such as failure and resemble are qualitative.

No population-level vertebrate dataset spans long-term evolution under doubled gravity.

Spaceflight data mostly concern microgravity, short duration and limited taxa.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.2
data existence: 0.3
analysis feasibility: 0.35
discriminating power: 0.4
operationalizability: 0.45

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: No existing dataset records terrestrial animals that evolved under doubled or halved gravity, so the literal prediction cannot be confirmed or refuted. Limb allometry against mass is a public proxy for the idea that gravitational load conditions form, and it is only a proxy: a short-legged large mammal is compatible with several selective stories. Discriminating power stays low for that reason.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: The doubled-gravity fauna is not in any dataset. A proxy is whether limb proportions become shorter and more heavily built as body weight, and thus skeletal load, increases. That pattern would support the scaling the counterfactual extrapolates; it would not show what animals would be like under twice or half Earth's gravity.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The claim is a counterfactual about a different gravitational constant.

Short legs have many ecological causes besides skeletal load.

fields.value:

data existence: 0.55
